candidate.text: You would rather teach yourself than be shown. You need to understand from the inside, so you teach yourself slowly, the private lesson ahead of the shared one. Say what you taught yourself out loud sometimes, since what you never explain stays yours alone.

angles.drive: Teaching yourself matters more to you than being taught. Needing to understand before you trust, you teach yourself from odd sources rather than take the standard lesson. Let someone teach you from time to time, since a lesson only you know is lonely.
angles.cost_self: Whenever you want to know something, you teach it to yourself instead of asking. Teaching yourself an answer costs you a month where being taught it costs an hour. Ask for the hour every so often, because you pay for each self-taught month in rest.
angles.cost_others: Rarely do you pass on the lesson you taught yourself. You taught it by a route too odd to explain, so you keep the knowing rather than tell it. Hand someone the messy version, because you leave anyone learning from you without the self-taught part.

candidate.text: Reading between the lines comes to you before reading the lines. You trust the read under a thing more than the proof, because what you take in sorts itself later. Give the proof a day, since you only share a read once it has words.

angles.drive: You read between the lines before you finish the lines. Needing to know a thing from underneath, you trust what sits between the words over what they say. Let the reason catch up before you act, since you cannot pass a hunch on without proof.
angles.cost_self: Between the lines is where you are quickest and hardest to follow. You go with the read rather than wait for proof, so the doubt stays yours. Write the read down, since you pay for every unchecked read in doubt about your own mind.
angles.cost_others: Whatever gets left between the lines, you read first and skip asking. Since your read lands before your question, you answer what sits under the words instead of the words. Ask the plain question, because you take from people the chance to say it themselves.

candidate.text: You think better alone than out loud. Since you hate being heard half-formed, you think a thing through alone rather than talk it through with help. Say one thought out loud before it is finished, because you only get help on thinking let out early.

angles.drive: Thinking alone is how you do your best thinking. Because you need the whole picture before you share any of it, you want the quiet ahead of the company. Take one invitation you usually turn down, since you give up company for thinking alone.
angles.cost_self: After a day of company, you need an hour of thinking alone to feel yourself. You think alone to fill up rather than hide, so you guard it over sleep. Guard the sleep too, since you take those hours from a night your body needed.
angles.cost_others: Your best thinking happens alone, and you go off to it without saying how long. Thinking best out of reach, you let the solo hours run long rather than stop early. Name the length first, since you give those waiting no time to expect you.

candidate.text: You calm people more than you ask to be calmed. Calming the people you love makes you feel useful, so you play the calm one, never the calmed one. Hand that part over for an evening, since you stay calm only when someone calms you.

angles.drive: Your presence calms people before your words do. Since you need people safe rather than impressed, you calm them with the slow question ahead of the fix. Let someone be the calm one for you sometimes, because you need calming as much as anyone.
angles.cost_self: Being the calm one comes naturally, and you forget it weighs anything. You calm someone through a bad month rather than admit your own, so you put yourself last. Say the tired thing out loud, since you pay for everyone's calm in rest not taken.
angles.cost_others: Whenever you watch someone close to you come apart, you become the calm under them. You calm them rather than get calmed, so you hide every shake of your own. Let them see you wobble, because you give them no chance to calm you back.

candidate.text: You keep the answers that worked and shelve the rest. Knowing what has worked matters to you ahead of what is new, so you change your mind slowly. Let one newer answer in each year, because you pay for the kept ones in chances missed.

angles.drive: Knowing what works comes easier to you than hoping something new will. Because you need an answer to have lasted, you reach for what has worked over what sounds clever. Give a new idea one honest try, since every answer you trust was new once.
angles.cost_self: Faced with a new way, you wait for proof rather than try it. Knowing what works means more to you than being early, so you land safe and late. Try one untested thing, because you miss the chances that wanted you early.
angles.cost_others: The advice you give has already worked somewhere. Knowing what works better than what someone hopes for, you send their new idea home with an old one. Hear the new idea out, since you take from them the chance to be wrong their own way.

candidate.text: Teaching at the other person's pace comes naturally to you. Because you put their understanding ahead of your speed, you teach it again rather than teach it louder. Let someone teach you slowly once in a while, since you are owed the patience you give.

angles.drive: You teach a thing a third time with the patience of the first. Needing the person to get there, you teach at their pace ahead of your own. Keep one hour a week that teaches nobody, because only you fill your patience back up.
angles.cost_self: Teaching someone patiently is easy for you and hard to count. Since you wait for them rather than hurry them, you hand your own evening to the lesson. Say no to one lesson a week, because you take every patient lesson out of your rest.
angles.cost_others: Your patience is what you teach with first. You teach it a second time instead of watching someone struggle, so you take the struggle that made it theirs. Let them not know a while longer, since you take the practice with every answer handed over.

candidate.text: You spot a chance early and trust the spotting. With Wood the energy you have least of, you spot the far thing ahead of the close one. Spot one near chance a week with the same care, since the far one keeps.

angles.drive: Spotting openings is what you do before anything is obvious. You carry less Wood than drive to spend, so you spot the far chance sooner than the one in your hand. Spot the near one as carefully, because it is yours to take.
angles.cost_self: Where you spot openings is always past where you stand. Wanting freedom more than settling, you spot what is far instead of taking what is near. Take a near one too, because each far chance you spot is a near one you let close.
angles.cost_others: You point out the openings you spot to whoever is near. Because the far chance holds you more than the near one, you spot the next before finishing this with them. Finish this one first, since spotting the next costs them some of your attention.

candidate.text: You start things early and without fuss, before any plan exists. Since waiting feels like losing time, you start the quick version ahead of the sure one. Start the way you do, and carry one start past where it stops being new.

angles.drive: Starting comes easily to you, often before you finish deciding. Moving is how you feel alive, so you start and learn rather than wait until you are sure. Keep starting freely, and let one start run long enough to teach you its ending.
angles.cost_self: Whenever something new opens, you start before asking what it takes. Starting feels like freedom, so you take the quick start ahead of the rest you are owed. Take the slow middle too, because every quick start costs you the rest you never take.
angles.cost_others: Whatever you start has other people in it before the thing is real. You need movement more than certainty, so you start, move on and leave the middle open. Stay for one ending, because each start you share leaves them the middle to finish.

candidate.text: You give before you count, and rarely regret it. Holding back feels like holding your breath, so you give to whoever needs it ahead of your own wants. Let one month have a plan as well, because a plan is how your generosity lasts.

angles.drive: Giving comes more easily to you than keeping, especially money. Being generous keeps the world feeling wide, so you give away a good month rather than save it. Keep giving, and hold one part back, because what you keep is what the giving stands on.
angles.cost_self: Giving is your first answer to most things. Being generous feels more like you than being careful, so you give the extra ahead of putting any aside. Give yourself a part too, because the money you never keep is what giving costs you.
angles.cost_others: Whenever the people close to you run short, you give before being asked. Giving keeps you freer than being owed, so you give rather than build anything shared. Let them give back sometimes, since your giving takes from them the chance to be generous too.

candidate.text: Whatever you build is made to last, in no hurry. Since you want a thing to last more than arrive first, you build it for years ahead of starting another. Celebrate halfway, because the patient years are the price you pay.

angles.drive: Building slowly is where you feel most sure of yourself. You have more push than Wood to put it into, so you build one thing for years rather than chase several. Keep building at that pace, because the slow build is the one you keep.
angles.cost_self: Whatever matters to you, you build for years. You put the built thing ahead of the wanted one, so you keep building what you have while your wish waits. Start building the wanted one too, because patience costs you the thing you never began.
angles.cost_others: You provide by building what lasts. Since you put finished ahead of shared, you build in private and keep the people near you waiting. Build one thing in plain sight, because the wait is the small price your care asks of them.

candidate.text: You save first and spend what is left, never as a sacrifice. Since money kept calms you more than money spent, you save before pleasure every time. Let pleasure win once in a while, because that is what the saving is for.

angles.drive: Saving comes before spending for you, and you never decide it. Being covered means more than anything you would buy, so you save ahead of wanting. Spend a small part of what you save on yourself, because a cushion is also for sitting on.
angles.cost_self: Your safety lives in what you have saved. Since you put feeling covered ahead of feeling alive, you save by postponing the small pleasures. Spend one of them on purpose, because saving first costs you the today you never have.
angles.cost_others: Whenever the people at home want something, you are already saving. Safety together matters more than happiness today, so you put saving ahead of the wish. Say yes to one wish early, because you are asking them to put a life on hold.

candidate.text: You stay loyal and count it as the love itself. Being someone's certainty feels better than being their surprise, so you keep being loyal ahead of being new. Be new for them sometimes, because you were chosen for more than your loyalty.

angles.drive: Being loyal comes ahead of being exciting for you. Being known feels safer than being wanted, so you stay loyal on dull days as much as good ones. Surprise the one you are loyal to once a year, because the same days are loyalty's price.
angles.cost_self: Where you gave your word, you stay loyal after the reasons change. Loyalty feels more like love than choosing, so you stop asking whether this is what you want or promised. Ask yourself every few years, because loyalty costs you the love you never chose.
angles.cost_others: Loyalty is how you love, given rather than said. You rate being loyal above speaking up, so you hand the person you keep your presence ahead of your feelings. Say it once in plain words, because unspoken loyalty leaves them guessing.

candidate.text: Wit is what you reach for first and would give up last. Wanting the quick true line said rather than the safe one, you pay more for silence than most people. Say the witty thing, and trust that you know when to hold it.

angles.drive: Your wit answers before your care does, and mostly you let it. Since being quick is how you know you are awake, you put the witty answer ahead of the careful one. Let the wit out, because you are kinder with it than you fear.
angles.cost_self: When talk gets hard, you reach the witty line before the honest one. You stay quick rather than get caught feeling something, so your wit lands where plain words belonged. Let plain words through, since each quick line costs you a piece of being known.
angles.cost_others: Saying the witty thing is how you take part. You get the laugh with the quick line rather than let one person finish, so you cost them being heard out. Hold the wit until their point lands, since your timing is good enough to wait.

candidate.text: The usual way is the one way you cannot bring yourself to do a thing. Because you want the original more than approval, you make the version you were not asked for. Keep making it, since the original is the one you are best at.

angles.drive: Doing a thing the usual way is nearly impossible for you, and only an original one feels done. Since you need things in pieces, you make your own version rather than follow the rule. Let originality count as talent, because it was never a fight.
angles.cost_self: Nothing feels real to you until you have made it original. You take being wrong your own way ahead of being right theirs, so you redo finished work. Count the originals that worked, because you paid for the rest in hours you never owed.
angles.cost_others: Making an original version of what you were handed shows you cared. You make someone's plan your own rather than follow it, so you deny them the small pride of a plan done as drawn. Carry one through unchanged sometimes, since your version can wait.

candidate.text: You speak up to the one doing it badly rather than around them. You would sooner be told you are wrong than left guessing, and you speak as plainly as you want to hear it. Stay plain, because speaking up is a kind of respect.

angles.drive: Not speaking up about something wrong is almost physically hard for you. You speak up ahead of being liked, because a true sentence left unsaid feels like a lie you took part in. Keep speaking up, since you are usually the only one who will.
angles.cost_self: Speaking up comes first, and counting the cost comes after. Being honest means more to you than comfort, so you speak up straight into fights you never meant to start. Leave one unsaid each month, because each unchosen fight costs you a friend's easy company.
angles.cost_others: When someone leaves a thing unsaid, you speak up about it as a kindness. You speak up rather than wait for them to work it out, so you use up the time they needed. Ask first, because true and welcome are not the same gift.

candidate.text: Giving is the first thing you do anywhere, before you know what is needed. Since being useful costs you less than being asked, you give care more than you ask for it. Keep giving freely, and count it as something you chose rather than owed.

angles.drive: Giving comes to you before anyone has asked, the most natural thing you do. Being needed feels closer to safe than being admired, so you give the help ahead of the ask. Keep giving first, because you were never giving to earn your place.
angles.cost_self: Where a need is in front of you, you give before asking whose it was. You keep giving ahead of wanting, so your own wants sit last in line. Let one person give to you, because you never get the pleasure you never ask for.
angles.cost_others: Long before the ask, you give people what they need. You give the answer rather than let the ones you love ask, so you leave them out of practice. Wait for the question sometimes, since being asked is also a way of being given to.

candidate.text: Your best work costs you no effort, and you keep waiting for it to feel harder. Because you trust forced work more than unforced, you hand over the easy thing with an apology. Hand it over without one, since the ease was the gift.

angles.drive: What you make comes out unforced, and you hardly notice how rare that is. Since effort is the only proof you trust, you put what you forced ahead of what came easily. Let the unforced thing count, because it was never the lesser one.
angles.cost_self: Whenever something comes to you without effort, you count it as worth less. You trust the forced version more than the easy one, so you add effort to finished work. Leave the unforced thing alone, because every hour spent forcing it is rest you lose.
angles.cost_others: Looking unforced is how you are kind to those you make things for. You hide the effort rather than show the care, so you keep them from knowing their worth to you. Let the effort show sometimes, since the care is the part worth keeping.

candidate.text: Wherever you sit down, you warm the place without announcing it. You want everyone to leave warmer rather than impressed, and you spend your words on comfort over show. Trust that warmth as something you make, because you are the one making it.

angles.drive: Warmth matters to you more than winning the point. You make the warmth around you on purpose, because an easy evening is where you are most yourself. Keep making it, and sit inside that warmth as a guest some evenings.
angles.cost_self: Keeping things warm for everyone comes before saying the hard thing. Since you keep the warmth rather than risk it on one honest sentence, you carry that sentence alone. Say it early, because staying warm costs you the one sentence you most need to say.
angles.cost_others: Each time something hard has to reach someone, you warm it first. You keep a child warm rather than tell them plainly what you saw, so you hold the plain version back. Give them the plain version sometimes, since the warmth was never in doubt.

candidate.text: Clear thinking comes to you most easily under pressure. Because you think this clearly nowhere else, you would sooner be tested under pressure than praised in comfort. Give yourself one hard thing a month, since you do your clearest work inside that pressure.

angles.drive: Pressure is where your thinking gets clear. Since you need certainty more than comfort, you let outside pressure clear your head rather than make your own calm. Choose some of that pressure yourself, because you are only this clear with something at stake.
angles.cost_self: Whenever the pressure lifts, your clear head goes with it and a quiet week feels like punishment. You would rather be clear under pressure than rested without it. Let one quiet week count as rest, because you trade the rest you need for clarity.
angles.cost_others: You bring pressure into calm places. Since you think more clearly under pressure, you put it on the people near you as much as yourself. Keep most of that pressure for yourself, because you take a calm evening from the people at home.

candidate.text: You end up in charge wherever the lead is open. You would sooner have anyone hold the lead than see it empty, so you take it on whenever nobody else will. Let someone else take charge, because you want things moving ahead of the title.

angles.drive: Taking charge comes to you before anyone offers it. Standing by while a group drifts feels worse than being wrong out loud, so you take charge before the vote. Hand the next one over, because you take charge better by choice than by habit.
angles.cost_self: Being in charge weighs on you once you take it. You feel safer in charge alone than sharing it, so you are rarely carried. Let one person carry part of it, because you pay for being in charge by never being looked after.
angles.cost_others: Wherever a plan stalls, you take charge and mean it kindly. Because a slow group feels risky, you take charge rather than wait your turn. Leave the next one to them, since each time you take charge you take their chance to decide.

candidate.text: You come alive the moment the stakes go up. Peace reads to you as being left out, so you keep the stakes high rather than settle for a sure thing. Choose those high stakes, because you are most yourself with something on the line.

angles.drive: Nothing at stake feels to you like being passed over. Since you only come awake with something to lose, you take high stakes over sure things. Keep one high-stakes thing going, because you were built to be tested rather than kept safe.
angles.cost_self: Loving high stakes means a calm stretch never feels like a reward. You would rather raise the stakes on something good than let it stay quietly good. Let one good thing stay low-stakes, because you keep spending the calm you could have kept.
angles.cost_others: When a day has no stakes, you add some. Since an easy win bores you more than a hard loss, you raise everyone's stakes with yours. Keep high stakes for your own plans, because you take the plain good day from those beside you.

candidate.text: You treat every promise as a contract with a witness. Since an outside standard keeps you steady, you keep the promise as much as the person you made it to. Reopen one promise a year, because you keep it long after it stops fitting.

angles.drive: Every promise you make becomes a rule you keep. Being relied on is the closest you get to feeling safe, so you keep your word ahead of your freedom to change it. Promise a little less freely, because you keep every one you make.
angles.cost_self: Keeping a promise costs you the right to change your mind. You would rather keep a stale promise than break it, so you stay inside plans past their use. Let yourself out of one, because you turn down better offers to keep old promises.
angles.cost_others: To you, a passing promise is one to keep. Because a promise is a rule rather than a wish, you hold everyone to every one they make. Let small promises go, since you leave your friends no freedom to have only been talking.

candidate.text: You feel most at home going by the book. Because an old rule holds you steady, you go the long way by the book rather than around it. Trust the book's slow route, since you are built for a standing that lasts.

angles.drive: By the book is the only way you trust a thing done. Since an outside rule steadies you, you go by the book ahead of the quick way. Stay with the book, because you are the standard the work gets checked against.
angles.cost_self: Where the book and your judgment part, you side with the book. You want it done in order more than your way, so you let the book decide what you knew. Allow the book one exception, because you give up chances that cannot wait.
angles.cost_others: Doing it by the book counts as respect paid forward. Because you want it right more than fast, you hold a friend's rushed job to the book too. Name the book out loud first, since you take the easy way from everyone beside you.

candidate.text: You want a title earned in full before enjoying it. Because you believe only a rank with work behind it, you take the title in writing over the thanks in passing. Enjoy the thanks too, since you earned it long ahead of the paperwork.

angles.drive: A fairly earned title is worth more to you than any praise. Since an earned rank says you belong, you earn the next title ahead of chasing the next thrill. Let the title come slowly, because you are already doing the job it names.
angles.cost_self: Earning the title comes first, claiming it long after. You want to look deserving more than to be paid, so you earn it twice before asking once. Claim it now, because earning it so slowly leaves money you were owed on the table.
angles.cost_others: Where titles are concerned, you make everyone earn theirs too. An unearned rank looks like cheating, so you give a colleague the long route rather than a quiet word. Say the word sometimes, because you take from them the years that earning costs.

candidate.text: Competing against someone moves you faster than any praise. Since you carry little Metal, you would rather borrow strength from a contest than from comfort. Compete with someone who also wants you to win, because you run a race that never announces a finish.

angles.drive: You compete best with someone to beat and know it. Knowing where you stand matters more than comfort, so you compete harder against one rival than for any reward. Pick one contest with a finish line, because you compete with no end in sight.
angles.cost_self: With no one to compete with, you lose your pace. Competing keeps you going, so the next round comes ahead of noticing you are tired. Compete against your own record for a month, since you never reach a finish that lets you rest.
angles.cost_others: For you, competing with a friend is taking them seriously. Since you want someone worth beating more than someone easy to keep, you raise the stakes. Keep one friend out of the contest, because you cost a rival the ease of siding with you.

candidate.text: Being first to bet is the part you enjoy. Betting first gives you strength where waiting gives none, and the bold move comes ahead of the sure one. Let one sure thing count, because you never count wins you did not bet on.

angles.drive: Your yes to a bet comes before the fear has finished. Hesitating feels like losing to yourself, so you bet first and size it afterwards. Keep one bet a year you can afford to lose, since nerve costs you money as much as pride.
angles.cost_self: Whenever the stakes go up, you are first to bet. Betting first is the closest you get to sure, so you size it to nerve rather than savings. Size one bet to the savings, since the early yes costs you money put aside.
angles.cost_others: Betting first is your way of carrying the people who hesitate. Since you bet for the group instead of asking it, you put their money where your nerve is. Check the size with them first, because you spend their caution like your own courage.

candidate.text: A shared risk is your fastest way into partnership. Being in it together matters more than being safe, and you split the stakes before the roles. Keep the roles clear, because you lose friends in a loose deal as easily as cash.

angles.drive: You trust a person faster once the risk is shared. Sharing the risk makes the bond real to you, so you go in together ahead of writing anything down. Write the terms down once, because you risk the friendship as much as the money.
angles.cost_self: Where a friend needs backing, you share the risk first. Sharing the risk feels closer than staying out, so the shared bet comes before your margin. Keep one account no friend can draw on, because you cover their losses with money meant for rest.
angles.cost_others: Sharing a risk with someone is your warmest offer. Since you want them in it more than safe from it, you share the upside and the fall. Say the downside first, because you bring the people you like into risks sized to your nerve.

candidate.text: The rules you live by are ones you made yourself. You make your own strength and put owing no one ahead of being carried. Let yourself be carried at times, since you built it all with no one placed to catch you.

angles.drive: You built your own standard with no one watching. Making a thing yourself feels safer than being measured on it, so you build alone rather than with help. Let one favour into the making, because you pay most for the things you make alone.
angles.cost_self: Whenever something matters, you make it yourself and let no one offer. Making it alone proves the standard is yours, so going without help comes ahead of going to bed. Ask for a hand early, because everything self-made costs you rest you never take.
angles.cost_others: Making everything yourself is what you show a new peer first. Since you make each thing alone instead of sharing, you leave your peers nothing to carry. Hand one piece over, because all you take from them is the chance to matter to you.

candidate.text: Your measure for yourself is your measure for everyone. Being even matters to you more than being liked, and you give the fair answer instead of the kind one. Offer the kind one more often, because you meet few who match your standard.

angles.drive: You hold everyone to the same measure as yourself. Fairness feels cleaner to you than favour, so being even with someone comes ahead of being easy on them. Let a friend off the hook sometimes, since you keep everyone you measure at a distance.
angles.cost_self: Whenever a friend falls short of the measure, you keep the measure rather than the friend. Holding everyone to one even measure keeps you honest. Bend it once for someone you like, because you spend long stretches without company that fits.
angles.cost_others: Being even-handed with a friend is how you show respect. Because you treat people you like exactly as yourself, you hand them your standard ahead of your warmth. Offer the warmth first, since you cost them the ease of being liked without being graded.

candidate.text: Being alone is how you recover and being around people is how you spend. With your Metal running short, you put the quiet you recover in ahead of any invitation. Try one invitation while tired, to see whether company counts as recovery.

angles.drive: Your strength recovers alone and gets spent in company. Being seen low feels like a debt you never repay, so you recover quietly instead of calling anyone. Let one person near while you are low, because you recover slower alone than you need to.
angles.cost_self: Out of sight is where you recover until whole again. Arriving half-built feels worse than arriving late, so you take the long quiet over the quick ask. Show someone the half-built version, as recovering alone costs you the friend who would have come.
angles.cost_others: Recovering alone spares the people near you your worst days. Since you return recovered instead of being seen recovering, you give them the finished version only. Let them in once while you recover, because you deny your closest people the chance to be needed.
